brief: A wide, completely FLAT plain (plaine) stretching to the horizon: flat green fields and meadow, a thin line of trees very far away, big blue sky. No hills at all, no mountains, no people, no text.
A deep valley (vallée): two tall steep mountains on the left and right, and a hollow between them with a small river at the bottom. Clearly a hollow between mountains. No people, no text.

A very wide, large river (fleuve), like the Saint Lawrence river: wide blue water flowing between two low green forested shores, seen from above at an angle. Clearly a big river, not a lake, not the sea. No boats, no people, no text.
A waterfall (chute) in a forest river: water falling from very high off a rocky cliff into a pool below, white foam at the bottom. No people, no boat, no text.
River rapids (rapides): a forest river with very agitated white foamy water rushing over many rocks, no waterfall, the river is mostly level but very rough. No people, no boat, no text.

Portage around river rapids in the year 1500: two original Indigenous Iroquoian adults (respectful, historically accurate clothing of deer skin) walking on a forest path beside a river, carrying a birchbark canoe upside down on their shoulders. The rapids are visible in the river next to them. Warm, dignified, friendly. No text.

An Iroquoian longhouse around the year 1500, seen from outside: a very long, narrow building with a rounded arched roof, much longer than wide, made of a wooden frame covered entirely with large sheets of brown tree bark, a small door at one end, smoke holes in the roof with a little smoke coming out. Grass around it. No people, no text.

Inside an Iroquoian longhouse around 1500: a long central aisle with a small cooking fire (hearth) on the floor in the middle, wooden sleeping platforms covered with furs along both walls, upper shelves with baskets, dried corn hanging from the roof beams, light coming from a smoke hole above the fire. Warm and cozy. No people, no text.

An Iroquoian village around 1500, seen from slightly above: several long bark-covered longhouses inside a tall wooden palisade (a fence of sharpened vertical tree trunks) that goes all around the village, with a single entrance gap, and a river with a birchbark canoe right next to the village. Corn fields outside the palisade. A few small original Indigenous people going about daily life, respectful and dignified. No text.
Three deciduous trees (feuillus) side by side: a maple tree, an oak tree and a white birch tree, with broad green leaves, round leafy crowns. No conifers at all. White background, no text.

Three coniferous trees (conifères) side by side: a fir, a spruce and a cedar, with needles, pointed triangular shapes, a few small brown pine cones visible. No leafy trees at all. White background, no text.

An original Iroquoian grandmother around 1500 (respectful, deer skin clothing) gently putting a crushed green medicinal plant on a child's scraped knee to heal it, a small basket of herbs and wild plants beside them, forest edge background. Clearly about healing with plants. Warm and kind. No text.
A birchbark basket full of wild food gathered in the forest: wild raspberries and blueberries, hazelnuts and walnuts, and a few brown forest mushrooms, on a mossy forest floor. No people, no text.

Clothing made from animals around 1500: a deer skin tunic with fringes, fur mittens, a fur-lined winter coat and a necklace made with feathers, displayed hanging on a wooden rack in front of a bark longhouse. Clearly clothes made from animal skins, furs and feathers. No people, no text.
